candidates.original_title: Correspondence of the brain's functional architecture during activation and rest
candidates.description: Correspondence between resting state and task brain networks
candidates.citation_sentence: In the present study, these Smith et al. main findings were highly reproducible using the HCP task and resting state data.
candidates.notes: The authors explicitly state the Smith et al. findings were 'replicable' and call it a 'true replication.' The replication uses different data (HCP COPE maps and resting-state ICA maps) and different analysis inputs (real task activation maps vs. BrainMap pseudo-activation maps), but preserves the core paradigm (group ICA + spatial cross-correlation of rest and task networks), warranting 'close experiment.'

candidates.original_title: Correspondence of the brain's functional architecture during activation and rest
candidates.description: Resting-state brain networks correspond to the functional networks engaged during task performance.
candidates.citation_sentence: In 2009, Smith et al. published a paper in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 30 that showed that the collection of brain networks that are 'active' while a person is resting and engaged in idle thought (e.g., resting state networks or RSNs) correspond to the same functional networks used by the brain to perform tasks.
candidates.notes: The paper explicitly states that the Smith et al. findings were highly reproducible and that this study provided a true replication, while also noting differences in subjects, stimuli, data inputs, and analysis methods.
